copyright: Polar bear cubs playing in Svalbard, Norway (© Danny Green/Nature Picture Library)
description: Two polar bear cubs pick their way across the snow in Svalbard, a remote Norwegian archipelago of glaciers, mountains and frozen fjords deep in the Arctic Ocean. This wild landscape is part of the Barents Sea region, home to one of the world's largest polar bear populations, with around 2,600 bears.

Evolution occasionally favours maximalism. Just look at these red-and-green macaws with their scarlet plumage, vivid green wings and blue flight feathers. Their lives unfold across tropical South America, in a routine that connects fruit, seeds and soil in ways that are easy to miss from the ground.

copyright: Field of kochia plants, China (© lingqi xie/Getty Images)
description: In today's image, kochia plants spread across the landscape in China in shades of green and deep red. Native to parts of Eurasia, kochia was introduced to the United States in the late 1800s as an ornamental plant and a source of material for broom making. Its ability to withstand drought, heat, saline soils and low rainfall helped it spread across the Great Plains and much of the American West.

copyright: Cadini di Misurina, Dolomites, Veneto, Italy (© Vithun Khamsong/Getty Images)
description: The image captures the jagged skyline of Cadini di Misurina at sunrise in Veneto, northeastern Italy. Visitors heading towards nearby Tre Cime di Lavaredo often come for the famous route only to find their attention hijacked by the Cadini. Part of the Dolomites, these needle-like peaks reaching more than 2,800 metres at their highest point seem sculpted for drama. The twist? They started out as ancient coral reefs.

copyright: Interior of the Royal Albert Hall, London (© William Barton/Shutterstock)
description: What happens when a grand classical concert lets its hair down? The Last Night of the Proms. The finale of the annual BBC Proms turns London's Royal Albert Hall into a joyful, flag-waving party, where world-class music meets quirky costumes, inflatable toys and enthusiastic singalongs.

copyright: The bay of Villefranche-sur-Mer, Alpes-Maritimes, Provence-Alpes-Côte d'Azur, France (© StockByM/Getty Images)
description: In September, the French Riviera is bathed in softer light, and the Mediterranean vegetation begins to regain its vibrancy. Along the coast, rosemary, wild thyme and Aleppo pine scent the air, while sailboats drift across the sheltered waters of Villefranche-sur-Mer.

copyright: Aerial view of Olvera, Andalusia, Spain (© Marco Bottigelli/Getty Images)
description: Ever wondered why Andalusia is one of Spain's best-known regions? Flamenco, tapas, Moorish architecture and extensive olive groves all play a part. Beyond its famous cities, you'll find historic places like Olvera. Surrounded by more than 2 million olive trees, this village developed as a strategic frontier settlement shaped by centuries of change. The Castle of Olvera still watches over the town, while the Church of Our Lady of the Incarnation dominates the skyline below. Visit La Cilla Cultural Center to discover Olvera's medieval history and traditions.
